case_number: Criminal Appeal No.4307 of 2024 (Arising out of SLP (Crl.) No.6166 of 2023)
summary: The appellant challenged the legality of conditions imposed during remission of his life sentence under Section 432(1) of CrPC. Conditions requiring 'decent behaviour' and automatic re-arrest upon cognizable offence allegation were contested as vague and arbitrary, violating Articles 14 and 21. Court examined scope of remission powers, conditionality, and constitutional limitations. Held that conditions must be clear, reasonable, and not amount to automatic revival of sentence without due process.
legal_provisions_cited: Shaikh Abdul Azees v. State of Karnataka
Union of India v. V. Sriharan alias Murugan & Ors
Epuru Sudhakar & Anr. v. Govt. of A.P. & Ors.
final_judgment: The Court struck down Conditions (1) and (2) as unconstitutional for vagueness and arbitrary consequences; upheld the power to impose reasonable, lawful conditions in remission orders.
